discovery: Development of next-generation DNA sequencing by sequencing-by-synthesis with reversibly terminated fluorescent nucleotides and clonal cluster amplification (Solexa/Illumina sequencing)
rationale: Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis rests on chemistry: reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry, surface cluster amplification and single-molecule fluorescence. It cut genome sequencing costs by orders of magnitude and changed biology and medicine. The work has already won the Breakthrough Prize (2022) and other major awards that often come before a Nobel. Recent Chemistry prizes (2024 protein design, 2025 MOFs) went to other fields, so a bio-analytical chemistry prize looks due.
